narrative: The model estimated that you have about a one-in-three chance of experiencing credit repayment problems, which is high enough under the bank’s decision rule to decline the application. This is a risk estimate, not a judgment that you will certainly default. The most influential factor overall was your checking account status. You have no checking account; because this is common among approved applicants, this factor actually worked in your favour and reduced the estimated risk. The most important factor working against you was your employment situation. You are currently unemployed, a status shared by only about 7% of approved applicants, and this pushed the assessment clearly toward bad credit risk. The third factor was your savings balance: having under 100 DM in savings added a smaller push toward bad risk. By contrast, your requested amount of 2,320 DM is below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, and your 18-month term is close to the 19-month average, so these did not drive the denial. To improve future chances, focus on stable employment and building savings before reapplying. You could also ask the lender whether a guarantor, co-applicant, smaller request, or proof of regular income would be considered, and reduce existing credit obligations where possible. Protected characteristics such as sex, age, and foreign-worker status were not used in this decision.
